articles.title: SJAA Club Activities and Meeting Information
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris outlines upcoming club activities from late November through January, including various star parties, dark sky weekends, and astronomy classes. It prominently features details for the December general meeting, where Dr. Robert Sabin will present his senior thesis on the stellar characteristics and evolutionary path of red giant stars. The document also provides contact information for the San Jose Astronomical Association and notes about additional events like a holiday party and board meetings.

articles.title: NASA Space Place: Projects for December 2008
articles.summary: This document presents the NASA Space Place calendar for December 2008, highlighting various astronomical events such as moon phases, the Geminids meteor shower, and the Winter Solstice. It also notes significant historical milestones in science and space exploration, like the invention of the microwave oven and Apollo 17's return. Each entry includes links to related educational projects and articles on the Space Place website, encouraging learning for children and educators.

articles.title: The Last Eclipse ... Ever?
articles.summary: This article explores the future of total solar eclipses, investigating when the Moon's recession from Earth due to tidal friction might prevent them entirely. Debunking a young-earth creationist argument, the author explains that the Moon's recession rate has not been constant and calculates that total solar eclipses could continue for approximately 664 million years. The piece concludes that eclipse enthusiasts have no immediate cause for concern and includes an astronomical ephemeris for December 2008.

articles.title: The Chemical Weather Report
articles.summary: Future weather reports are expected to evolve into "chemical weather forecasting," providing daily air quality predictions based on satellite observations of atmospheric pollutants. NASA's Aura satellite, equipped with instruments like the Tropospheric Emission Spectrometer, currently tracks gases such as ozone and carbon monoxide using spectrometry. A proposed GEOCAPE satellite in geosynchronous orbit would offer continuous monitoring, enabling daily air quality forecasts to help people plan around dangerous conditions.

articles.title: Barack Obama and Science
articles.summary: This editorial analyzes President-elect Barack Obama's views on science and its potential impact on science education and research in the United States. It highlights his strong scores on science-related issues, his commitment to increasing federal funding for basic research, and his support for STEM education, contrasting his stance with previous administrations and other political figures. Despite high hopes from the scientific community, the article acknowledges that economic challenges might temper immediate significant budget increases.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: This article, 'The Last Month In Astronomy,' provides a concise roundup of significant astronomical news from late October to mid-November 2008. Key updates include the Space Shuttle Endeavour launch, the first visible-light image of an extrasolar planet, the completion of the Phoenix Mars Lander's mission, and the Hubble Space Telescope's return to service. It also highlights new observations of Enceladus, the Epsilon Eridani system, and glacier melt data, concluding with an announcement for a holiday party.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a Telescope Loaner Program, allowing members to try various telescopes ranging from binoculars to large Dobs before committing to a purchase. The article also provides a comprehensive directory of the club's officers, board of directors, and staff, along with their contact information via phone and email. Additionally, it details the publication schedule and formats for the club's monthly newsletter, the SJAA Ephemeris.
